originalTitle: Australia news live: Pauline Hanson opposes major gun buyback agreed in wake of Bondi terror attack
content: ‘Additional arrangements’ being worked on for children removed from NDIS, minister says Asked what happens to a nine-year-old who is removed from the NDIS, McAllister said: We will need to work through the additional Foundational Supports. There’s $10bn that premiers and the prime minister have agreed ought to be applied to standing up Foundational Supports. We started with children, but we know that we’ll need to stand up … and make additional arrangements. NDIS minister says Thriving Kids scheme on track to commence from 1 October The minister for disability and the NDIS, Jenny McAllister, has been on Insiders, where she was asked about Thriving Kids, which states and territories will start rolling out on 1 October. She said: We are, in every other state, seeing the states getting moving, and I’m really confident – having met with state and territory counterparts on Friday – that we will see these states ready to move. Richard Marles is visiting Port Moresby and Honiara this weekend, meeting with Papua New Guinea’s prime minister, James Marape, and defence minister, Elias Kapavore, today. Discussions will focus on strengthening defence cooperation and advancing implementation of the historic Pukpuk treaty. Marles will then head to Solomon Islands and meet with the country’s prime minister, Matthew Wale, and join government ministers at the opening of the Western Border Outpost in the Shortland Islands. The facility will bring together police, customs, immigration and biosecurity officials in one location, and support Solomon Islands’ Guardian-class patrol boats. “Pacific security is most effective when it is led by Pacific nations,” Marles said. Australia is proud to work alongside our Pacific partners to support their priorities and contribute to a secure, stable and resilient region. ‘I don’t like the gay Mardi Gras’: Hanson Pauline Hanson has renewed her criticism of the Sydney gay and lesbian Mardi Gras, saying she doesn’t like the annual event. Back in her first stint in federal politics, Hanson told journalist Tracey Curro that she believed the event promoted something that is “unnatural”. On Sunday, she said gay marriage was legal in Australia, describing it as “acceptable”. “I still don’t like the gay Mardi Gras, but that’s my opinion,” she said. I think your own personal sexuality should be kept in closed doors, behind closed doors. It’s no one’s business to do it out there with the gay Mardi Gras anywhere. I know it brings a lot of tourists to the country. I know it brings a lot of money. I know all this, but that’s my personal opinion. But anyway, good luck to them that they want to do that. The comments come after One Nation MP Barnaby Joyce claimed the party was one of “the gayest” in federal politics last week. Sydney’s Mardi Gras has been going since 1978. Starting as a gay rights protest, marking the anniversary of New York’s Stonewall uprising, the parade was a protest against homophobia and police brutality. Some history here: Thai prime minister to visit Canberra Anthony Albanese says his Thai counterpart, Anutin Charnvirakul, will visit Australia this week. The two leaders will meet in Canberra on Wednesday to discuss deepening economic cooperation. The visit will be Prime Minister Anutin’s first to Australia since taking office. Albanese said: Australia and Thailand enjoy a warm relationship, built on trust and a shared commitment to a prosperous Indo-Pacific. Many Australians have experienced Thailand’s warmth and hospitality through travel, while the Thai-Australian community continues to enrich our nation and strengthen the enduring ties between our countries through business and culture. Hanson wants to slash international student numbers One Nation leader Pauline Hanson says she wants dramatic cuts to the number of international students allowed to come into the country. Hanson is refusing to say how much overseas migration should be cut, but agrees with News24 host Andrew Clennell that she wants to slash overseas student numbers. “I think the international student industry that’s been set up by the universities is a farce,” she said. People are using it to come to the country. Then after they get in the country, they’re only here for a few months. Then they change the courses. Then they apply for residence here in Australia. So they’re using [it] as a back door to get into the country. Pauline Hanson says she is opposed to a major gun buyback being announced by Anthony Albanese and the NSW premier, Chris Minns, in Sydney shortly. Legislation for the plan passed parliament earlier this year, part of the response to the Bondi beach terror attack. It will be run in two phases, with the cost split 50:50 between the federal and NSW governments. Under the first phase of the scheme, $1,000 will be paid for revolvers and $850 for semi-automatic handguns. Compensation of $850 will be paid for double-barrel shotguns and $650 for those with a single barrel. Between $650 and $1,000 will be paid for rifles, while air rifles have a fixed compensation of $450. Hanson told News24 taxpayers should not pay for the scheme. She suggested the buyback would impact “law-abiding Australians who are trying to go about their business, like farmers that need their guns,” she said. A different gun is for a different purpose, and you have to understand guns. I’ve got my own gun licence, so I understand these people. Good morning. There is a bit of news around today. An agreement has been struck on a major federal-state gun buyback in response to the Bondi terror attack. The commonwealth and NSW governments will evenly share the cost of the scheme. National cabinet agreed to fight antisemitism and strengthen firearms restrictions across the nation after the deadly December 2025 shooting. We’re expecting to hear from the prime minister, Anthony Albanese, and NSW premier, Chris Minns, soon. chineseTitle: 澳大利亚新闻直播：宝琳·汉森反对邦迪恐怖袭击后同意的重大枪支回购
chineseContent: 部长表示，正在为从 NDIS 中除名的儿童制定“额外安排”。当被问及从 NDIS 中除名的 9 岁儿童会发生什么时，麦卡利斯特说：我们需要通过额外的基础支持来开展工作。州长和总理已同意拨款 100 亿美元用于建立基础支持。我们从孩子们开始，但我们知道我们需要站起来……并做出额外的安排。 NDIS 部长表示 Thriving Kids 计划将于 10 月 1 日开始实施 残疾和 NDIS 部长 Jenny McAllister 在 Insiders 节目中被问及 Thriving Kids 计划，该计划将于 10 月 1 日开始在各州和领地推出。她说：我们在其他每个州都看到这些州正在采取行动，我非常有信心——在周五与州和领地同行会面后——我们将看到这些州准备好采取行动。理查德·马尔斯将于本周末访问莫尔兹比港和霍尼亚拉，并于今天会见巴布亚新几内亚总理詹姆斯·马拉佩和国防部长埃利亚斯·卡帕沃尔。讨论将集中于加强防务合作和推进历史性普克普克条约的实施。随后，马勒斯将前往所罗门群岛，会见该国总理马修·韦尔，并与政府部长一起出席肖特兰群岛西部边境前哨基地的启用仪式。该设施将把警察、海关、移民和生物安全官员聚集在一个地点，并为所罗门群岛的卫报级巡逻艇提供支持。马勒斯说：“太平洋安全由太平洋国家领导时最为有效。”澳大利亚很自豪能够与我们的太平洋伙伴合作，支持他们的优先事项，并为建立安全、稳定和安全的环境做出贡献。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
